newsitem.title: USA: Dlr/yen ends up in U.S., retains overnight gains.
newsitem.headline: Dlr/yen ends up in U.S., retains overnight gains.

text.p: The dollar retained most of its overnight gains against the yen despite disappointing U.S. trade data which briefly hurt the dollar against most other major currencies, analysts said.

The dollar soared to a 33-month high of 112.63 yen overnight after the Ministry of Finance said Japan's trade surplus for goods cleared of customs tumbled 30.3 percent to 779.52 billion yen in September from a year earlier.
However, a greater-than-expected August deficit in U.S. international trade flows capped the dollar's rise against the yen and sent the dollar lower against the mark, dealers said.
The dollar closed at 112.55/60 yen, up from 112.44/49 at Friday's open. Against the mark, the dollar ended little changed at 1.5418/23 compared to 1.5419/22 at the open.
Economists had expected a significant contraction in the August numbers after the trade gap ballooned in July to a revised $11.60 billion, the highest monthly shortfall since the end of 1987.
An increase in imported Chinese Christmas decorations and toys bumped the overall August trade gap to $10.83 billion, exceeding the consensus view for an $8.4 billion shortfall.
"The dollar sold off originally against the mark in particular because the trade number was a disappointment," said Tom Benfer, director of foreign exchange at the Bank of Montreal in New York.
"But it didn't really have a strong and lasting impact on the dollar, which remained fairly well-bid."
A surge in sterling against the mark to a 22-month high at 2.4568 helped the dollar recover lost ground against the mark after the U.S. trade report, dealers said.
Comments from Tim Congdon, a member of the UK Treasury panel of independent economic advisers, combined with new data showing a spurt in UK broad money growth in September boosted the pound.
Congdon called for a full percentage point increase in official interest rates from the current 5.75 percent rate to stave off what he sees as the threat of resurgent inflation.

The Bank of England has been calling since July for a rise in UK interest rates to 6.0 percent, but Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke, who has cut rates four times since December, has so far rejected the bank's advice.
In late trade, the dollar held firm after news Russian President Boris Yeltsin fired Russian armed forces chief of staff General Mikhail Kolesnikov.
Kolesnikov had no known links with former security chief Alexander Lebed, whom Yeltsin sacked on Thursday in an attempt to crush an escalating Kremlin power struggle.
The dollar surged against the mark on Thursday after Lebed's dismissal.

In other trade, sterling gained to $1.5890/00 from $1.5860/65 at Friday's open. The dollar rose to 1.2701/06 Swiss francs from 1.2690/95 on Friday and fell to Canadian $1.3485/90 from C$1.3521/26. The Australian dollar rose to $0.7955/60 from $0.7946/51 at the open.
